name: Comet
notes: Comet is famous around the shelter for napping up to eighteen hours a day and rarely barking, which makes him surprisingly easy to live with in a smaller space. He only needs a couple of short walks to stay content, though he still lights up at the sight of an open field to stretch his legs. His strong instinct to chase small, fast-moving animals means a cat-free household is best for him.

name: Blitz
notes: Blitz is happiest when he has a job to do, whether that's agility drills, advanced obedience work, or helping herd the shelter volunteers into a line. He's whip-smart and can get a bit too creative with his energy if left without structure, so an experienced handler who can keep up with him is a must. He tends to fixate on cats given the chance, so feline-free households suit him better.

name: Sadie
notes: Sadie was bred to guard livestock independently through the night, and that watchful, self-directed nature carries over into her personality today. She's remarkably gentle and patient with the children she's met at the shelter, and she shares a yard peacefully with the resident cats. She can be standoffish with unfamiliar dogs on walks, so a home without other resident dogs is the best fit.

name: Zeus
notes: Zeus forms an intensely loyal bond with his person but takes a long time to warm up to anyone new, including unfamiliar dogs and small children whose quick movements make him uneasy. Oddly enough, he's completely unbothered by the laid-back shelter cat he shares a yard with. He needs a confident, patient handler willing to work through his wariness at his own pace.

name: Wrigley
notes: Wrigley trots through his days like he owns the place, greeting every dog, cat, and human at the shelter with equal enthusiasm. He's quick to learn new tricks when food is involved and still needs some polishing on impulse control around the treat jar. His short legs don't slow him down one bit on family walks or games of chase in the yard.

name: Nova
notes: Nova is a talkative, independent-minded girl who isn't afraid to voice her opinion with a full range of howls and grumbles. She's a talented escape artist who needs secure fencing and an adopter who won't take her stubborn streak personally, though she's genuinely social and affectionate on her own terms. Her strong prey drive means she isn't a match for homes with cats.

name: Daisy
notes: Daisy still lights up like a puppy whenever a new scent trail crosses her path, and sniffing walks around the block are her favorite part of the day. She settles down easily indoors afterward and has shared a yard with the shelter's resident cats without any drama. Her easygoing, food-motivated nature makes her a forgiving first dog for a new adopter.

name: Rocky
notes: Rocky is a bouncy adolescent who greets the world with his whole body and hasn't quite learned his own strength yet. He needs daily runs and consistent training to channel his enthusiasm, and he shines in daycare-style playgroups with other high-energy dogs. He gets overly excited around cats, so a cat-free home is the better fit.

name: Whiskers
notes: Whiskers spends her afternoons stalking feather toys and keeping a close watch on the birds outside the window. After a stressful experience with a dog in a previous home, she does best without canine roommates, though she gets along easily with the other shelter cats. She warms up to new people quickly once she's had a chance to explore every corner of a room.

name: Shadow
notes: Shadow goes fully limp with contentment the moment he's picked up, living up to his breed's reputation for being endlessly easygoing. He spends most afternoons napping in a sunny window and has adjusted comfortably to sharing space with both dogs and other cats at the shelter. He prefers slow head scratches and quiet company over rowdy play sessions.

name: Simba
notes: Simba is a large, athletic climber who needs tall cat trees and plenty of vertical space to patrol throughout the day, which makes a compact apartment a tough fit for him. He greets guests at the door almost like a dog and loves a good interactive wand-toy session. After some territorial spats with shelter roommates, he does best as the only cat in the home.

name: Biscuit
notes: Biscuit is a dignified senior who takes his time trusting new faces and prefers a slow, predictable routine over sudden changes. He can be startled by the unpredictable energy of young children, so a quieter adult household suits him best, though he's lived comfortably alongside both a calm dog and another cat at the shelter. Once he bonds with someone, he follows them from room to room.

name: Nala
notes: Nala struts through the shelter like she's already found her forever home, greeting every visitor with a confident head-bump and a loud purr. She's still working on her manners around the food bowl and can be a little pushy with slower-moving cats, though consistent routines have already started to help. She'd love a household with plenty of company throughout the day.

name: Oliver
notes: Oliver is a reserved, watchful cat who needs a slow introduction period and a calm environment to feel secure. After rocky introductions with both a dog and another cat at the shelter, he's made it clear he prefers being the only pet in the household. He's deeply affectionate with his person once he trusts them, following them quietly from room to room rather than demanding attention.
